The HCBS Relief Act of 2025 throws billions at Medicaid's structural failures while ignoring the root causes. Section 2(a)(1) increases federal matching funds by 10% for home care services without mandating eligibility audits or anti-fraud measures - a blank check for bureaucratic bloat. Massachusetts already burned through $3.7B in Medicaid funding last year while 48% of LEP patients faced dangerous medical errors.

Congressman Auchincloss' push for "flexibility" misses the point. States don't need new waivers - they need to stop hemorrhaging cash through duplicate programs and ER misuse by non-citizens. The bill's Section 2(b)(2)(B) requires states to maintain existing spending levels, guaranteeing that any new funds will layer onto existing waste rather than replace it.

Real reform would sunset failed programs, enforce immigration status verification for Medicaid enrollment, and redirect savings to veterans' care. Until Washington stops treating Medicaid as a slush fund for political pet projects, no amount of "collaboration" will fix this broken system.
